story_type: hurricane flood hoist: pararescueman rides the cable up with a toddler, kids and a woman flown to a dry parking lot
hook: He rose out of Harvey's floodwater holding a little girl.
narration: A pararescueman rose out of Harvey's floodwater, holding this little girl.
Hurricane Harvey had put whole neighborhoods near Houston under water.
A New York Air National Guard crew from the 106th Rescue Wing flew in.
The pilots can't see straight below, so the crew in the open door talk them over the house and run the hoist.
First, a boy came up the cable and into the cabin.
Then the pararescueman rode down again, to a building cut off by the flood.
[short pause] He came back up with the girl in his arms, and went out once more.
Inside, a woman held the girl close as the Pave Hawk flew out over the flood.
It set down in a dry parking lot.
outcome: Everyone aboard stepped off the helicopter and walked out onto dry ground.
title: Toddler lifted out of Harvey's flood
description:
After Hurricane Harvey in 2017, pararescuemen from the 106th Rescue Wing, New York Air National Guard, flew search and rescue missions from an HH-60 Pave Hawk near Houston, Texas, lifting children and adults out of flooded neighborhoods.

Footage: U.S. Air Force video by Senior Airman Joshua Hoskins, Air Force Public Affairs Agency, via DVIDS: https://www.dvidshub.net/video/547567/hurricane-harvey-relief
